note: Report only: these rules give a pull request a tier (issue #3393). Nothing reads them yet to block, label or merge; T3 needs a human, and the final merge policy is decided in stage 5 of #3393. Editing this file is itself T3 (`.github/**`). Paths are matched in the fixed order T3 -> T2 -> T1 -> T0, first match wins, so a broader lower tier never shadows a narrower higher one: keep the lists non-overlapping when they cover the same directory.

T3.meaning: high risk: the automation itself, the vendored upstream, dependency and deploy manifests, secrets and auth code. Green CI is not enough; a human approves.

T2.meaning: medium risk: service, runtime and manager code, and any path no rule names (never silently T0/T1).

T1.meaning: low risk: client code, tests and the checked-in static pages.

docsCodeNote: T0 is for prose: a code file under docs/ or changelog.d/ is T2, like any path no rule names, so a new script added there is not silently T0 while a .md next to it still is (issue #3393). A new script with no extension is caught by its patch as well: a file added under a `shebangPaths` tree whose added lines start with a shebang is T2, including a name like `docs/deploy` (see `shebangNote`).
shebangNote: Every path list above is an extension or a directory, so a name with no extension is invisible to them; the patch is what says it is a script. A file added under one of these trees with an added line that starts with a shebang is T2. Only an added file is read (an existing shebang is not in the patch), and a name with an extension is left to the lists above, so a .md that quotes a shebang in a fence stays documentation. Known limit: a new script with neither a shebang nor an extension stays T0 (#3393).
generatedPathsNote: The built browser half of the vendored ds-bot (3.2 MB, `Generated from src/client ... Do not edit by hand`); it is inside the vendor tree and so T3 by path anyway, this only keeps the size count honest. The old layout kept the same build output twice, as `core/client.js` and `ds-bot/client.js`, so both are listed.
limitsNote: Recomputed for the 0.3.0 tree. Sample of six changes in the new layout (five merged, one open): #3390 5L/1F, #3389 54L/5F, #3386 280L/11F, #3391 386L/13F, #3382 633L/7F, #3388 1128L/14F. The old caps (T0 300/15, T1 400/20, T2 250/12) were sized for the pre-0.3.0 layout, where the largest such change was under 400 lines; here the largest real UI change is #3388 at 1128L/14F, which the old T1 cap would have called T3. So: T2 keeps #3382 (633L/7F) and #3391 (386L/13F) at T2 with margin; T1 keeps #3388 at T1; T0 doubles the docs budget for a full doc rewrite. Going over a cap still means T3 (a human looks), which is the safe direction; T3 has no cap of its own.
